subject: dwarfBlacksmith
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf blacksmith at an anvil.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm designing a compact but detailed dwarf blacksmith model with Warcraft-style proportions—chunky build, pauldrons, braided beard, leather apron, hammer and glowing anvil—while planning a sensible joint hierarchy covering hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, arms, and legs, aiming to keep the whole module around 250 lines with correct API usage.

Mapping out the skeleton coordinates: hips, spine chain using catmull curves up to the chest, neck and head joints, and torso built via a sweep over the spine chain with a wider radius for the bulky frame, then setting up symmetric leg limbs with hip and foot positions.

Adjusting leg lengths so the hip-to-foot distance matches properly, naming joints per side with the L/R suffix, sweeping thick radii for the legs, and boxing in boot geometry at the feet. Now I'm positioning the shoulders symmetrically and planning the arm/hand setup, with one hand gripping a raised hammer.

For the resting arm pose, I'm extending them slightly down-forward with calculated distances to keep elbow bends within reach, setting up shoulder/elbow/wrist chains and swept radii, adding sphere fists at the wrists, and designing spiked pauldrons with metal paint for the armor look.

Now I'm placing a hammer in the right hand with a vertical rod handle and a box-shaped head oriented along the x-axis, leaving the left hand empty, then building the head: a scaled skull sphere, a pinkish nose sphere, and planning textured eye planes facing forward.

I'm figuring out where to decal the eyes onto the skull surface using the part's geometry, then sketching brow boxes and a lathe-based dwarf helmet dome with horns that sits above the eyes and covers the top of the skull.

Still shaping the beard geometry...

For the jaw I'm setting up a joint with upper and lower bone pieces, hiding the mouth mostly behind the beard. Then I'm building the leather apron as a box attached to the torso front, adding painted burn marks near the bottom, and figuring out how to construct the belt loop.

I'm weighing options for the belt shape -- trying a lathe-based ring approximating the torso's elliptical cross-section, since scaling isn't straightforward on lathe parts, so I'm adjusting the torso radii to be more uniformly round instead.

Still planning the figure's dimensions...

Finishing the anvil waist and top dimensions, then adding a glowing iron bar on top for the forging effect plus some spark particles. I'm also positioning the stump and hands so everything lines up at the right depth, and considering a rune decal for the apron.

Now I'm sorting out the material palette: mottled skin, leather, and metals for iron, gilt, steel, and bronze pulled from the clockwork kit, plus a glow paint for effects. I'm settling on importing the core builder utilities—createBuilder, rng, mottle, grain, paint—directly from the main package.

For the skeleton, I'm skipping a separate neck chain and instead attaching a neck joint to the chest, with the head parented to the neck, then sweeping a short tapered shape between them for the neck geometry.

For the torso, I want shirt cloth coloring in a dark red-brown, but I need to switch the sweep caps to flat instead of round since round caps extend the radius beyond the path endpoints and would push into the head/chin area. I'm adjusting the spine path to end around y=1.15 with flat caps so the shoulder sphere can properly cover the transition, and setting legs to start at the hip height with flat caps too to avoid overlap artifacts with the torso.

Now I'm positioning the shoulder joints and pauldron armor pieces: placing shoulder spheres at the sides, adding hemisphere pauldrons using a partial sphere geometry so the dome faces upward and the bottom stays open, then topping each pauldron with a small spike for decoration. Checking the vertical placement so the spike sits correctly above the pauldron's dome height.

I'm also adding a thin trim ring around each pauldron using a rotated torus geometry, and setting up left/right naming for bones based on side. Next I'm wiring up hand positions for the hammer using the wrist joint tip of the arm chain, and planning the leg sweep geometry for boots using the limb's bone chain as the sweep source.

For the dwarf's arms, I'm adding bare forearm skin plus steel bracer cylinders positioned between elbow and wrist using interpolation, and sketching out a small glowing spark sphere attached near the hand.

I'm deciding to anchor all the props to the hips bone for simplicity, and making sure boots and the leg stump both touch the ground at y=0. Then I'm sketching the eyes, nose with veins, small ear spheres, and cheeks, and working out a beard shape using a swept path with a tapering radius function that narrows toward the tip.

Writing beard texture and braid sweeps...

I'm scaling an ellipsoid helper for hair geometry, then adding a small noseguard box, a gilt rim ring, and a glowing red gem to the helmet. I'm setting up a wrapper function for placing meshes onto bones, and starting a lathe profile for the helmet shape that needs to form a closed loop from axis to back and around.

I'm checking that the helmet radius clears the skull geometry at the base and brow positions, verifying the math on ellipsoid cross-sections so the helmet doesn't clip into the head. Now I'm positioning eye decals and starting to build a rotated box for the brows.

Working out the brow rotation so each side angles inward correctly, with outer ends higher and inner ends lower, while checking clearance between the brow, eye, and nose positions relative to the helmet base before writing out the full component code.
